title: Credential value present only in a Base64 or hex form
description: An authored base value (a credential-shaped literal) whose bytes appear in the input only after one Base64 or Base16 (hex) encoding, alone in a field or inside other text. Terms: standard Base64 uses '+' and '/', URL-safe Base64 uses '-' and '_' in their place (RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5); padded text ends in '=' to a multiple of four characters, unpadded text omits it; hex is lower, upper or mixed case; whole-value means the encoded text is the entire value of its field, embedded means it sits inside longer text; single layer means one encoding of the base value. For an ASCII base the two Base64 alphabets give identical text unless the base holds '>' or '~' (which encode to '+') or '?' (which encodes to '/') at a byte offset whose remainder modulo three is two, and padding appears only when the base length is not a multiple of three.
semantics: Four questions are kept apart: (1) observation, whether anything reports on the input; (2) decoded-family recognition; (3) source coverage, whether a reported range covers the encoded source span that stands for the base; (4) actual-output protection. Policy (maintainer-only, ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 2): when the decoded base is a credential, the whole encoded text is the secret range and the outcome is must-flag; the fixture facts are the authored base, the encodings in order, the decoded digest and length, and the byte range of the encoded text. Whether a decoder runs, and the action taken, are decisions of the owning product and are not stated by any fixture of this scenario. A decoder succeeding on a value never makes that value a secret: encoded hashes, public text and placeholders are the benign counterparts and project their own benign Case or Scenario.

applicability.rationale: The reasoning is the same for every family and for provider-less literals: only the base value differs, so it is stated once and instantiated by a plan over authored bases.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 2 (#94)): when the decoded base is a credential, the whole encoded text is the range and the outcome is must-flag. RFC 4648 defines the encodings and says nothing about confidentiality; the rule is a project choice, not a provider fact. Decoder support, depth, expansion and size limits and the action taken are the product's. The benign twins (a decoded base that is not a credential) stay must-not-flag under the same policy. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Defines the standard Base64 alphabet, the URL and filename safe alphabet that replaces '+' and '/' with '-' and '_', when padding may be omitted, and Base16 as hexadecimal digits; implementations reject characters outside the alphabet.
